active_work_package.title: Platform repository skeleton from the P0.2 design
active_work_package.objective: Create the place every later package lands, shaped so the modular monolith boundaries are tested rather than intended: the workspace and layout, the module registry, the seven dependency rules generated from it, the migration lint, the boundary test suite that proves both fire, the charter, these records and their schemas, and the CI skeleton. It implements no epic and creates no domain table.

known_divergence: The boundary rules here are the PROPOSAL of a design at IN_REVIEW that depends on five ADRs, none of them accepted (ADR-001, ADR-004 and ADR-010 are PROPOSED; ADR-005 and ADR-011 are DRAFT_REQUIRED). TEN review rounds have now been held (issue 8), and the defect class they keep finding has never once been a wrong rule: the suite was green while a rule did nothing. What round five adds is that the defect was never measurable before - the instrument that was supposed to detect it reported a number inflated by exactly the overlap it could not see. DEC-027 makes the unit of coverage the control that actually discriminates, and the cost is now visible rather than hidden: 193 mutations 'all caught' honestly reads as 146 with an exclusive killer plus 47 that no fixture distinguishes. THREE THINGS ARE WORTH STATING PLAINLY. First, this repository has now put its own defect class INSIDE the instrument built to detect that class four separate times - the coverage gate's environment seam, the attribution gate's own verdict wiring, the shallow-history guard, and the accepted_keys rule chain. Each was caught by a review reading the whole rather than the change. Second, a reviewer twice built the evidence an implementer had declared impractical to build, and each time the evidence contradicted the implementer's conclusion - once proving a bypass three separate written claims denied could exist. Third, and this is the one that bounds everything above: the signing check is DETECTION, not prevention, and it is unenforced today. Nothing mechanically distinguishes a human enrolment from an agent one, because any check the agent can edit is a check the agent can edit. Only required_signatures branch protection on main - a human act, on GitHub, outside this repository - converts it into a binding. The residual named in DEC-021 is therefore narrowed rather than closed. A consistent forgery across the governance records still passes every check here. What changed is that the repository now says so in a distinct, greppable word on every single run, and carries the mechanism that would end it the moment a human enrols a key.
